transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I guess what finally made me come in is my wife’s been getting pretty frustrated with me. She’ll be telling me things—like about my cousin’s appointments, or who needs a ride where—and I’m looking right at her, nodding along, and then a minute later I realize I didn’t actually catch half of what she said.

And it’s not that I don’t care, you know? I mean, my cousin’s had a lot going on, and there’s always some schedule to keep straight. My wife is good at that kind of thing—she’ll remember times and names and all that. But I’ll be sitting there like I’m listening, and then it’s just… gone, or it didn’t really go in. That’s been bothering me.

Has this trouble staying focused and retaining what people say been something you've noticed since childhood or your teenage years, or is this a new change for you, say within the last several months?

No, it’s not really new. I mean, it feels more noticeable now because my wife is the one getting annoyed with it, and there’s all these appointments and family stuff to keep straight, but… yeah, it goes way back.

Even in grade school, before I was 12, I remember teachers telling my parents I was bright, but I was always off in my own head. Daydreaming, you know. And I’d leave homework sitting in my desk and then come home like, “Oh, I forgot it,” and my mom would get that look. Teachers had to remind me to finish classwork too. Funny, I can still picture the inside of that old desk, with the pencil grooves and all—sorry, anyway. Yeah, it’s been around since I was a kid.
Growing up, and even now, have you also struggled with being restless, fidgety, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Um… I don’t know. Not really in a way that stands out to me, I guess.

I mean, I’ll shift around in a chair sometimes, but who doesn’t, right? My dad used to tap his fingers on the kitchen table and it drove my mother crazy—funny how you remember stuff like that. But as far as, like, being the kid who couldn’t sit still or was always blurting things out… I don’t think that was really me.

The impulsive thing, I’m not sure. I can make a dumb decision now and then, sure, but I wouldn’t say that’s been the main issue. It’s more… well, I’m not sure that’s what people have complained about with me.
Do you often find yourself losing track of important items, missing deadlines, or struggling to keep your daily tasks and belongings organized?

Yeah, the losing things part, definitely. I’ll set down my keys or my phone somewhere in the house and then I’m wandering around retracing my steps for ten minutes, checking the same counter twice. It’s ridiculous sometimes.

And not just those—like, I had these catering receipts once, or garden clippers when I’m out doing yard stuff, and I’ll put them “somewhere obvious,” supposedly, and then they’re just gone. Well, not gone, obviously, they’re usually on a shelf or by the back door or something. But it turns into this whole little search mission, and I get annoyed with myself.
Would you say these attention and organization struggles have caused real problems for you not just at home, but also at work or in other areas of your life?

Yeah… I’d say it has, not like everything’s falling apart, but it’s causing some real friction.

At home, my wife gets frustrated because she feels like she can’t fully count on me with my cousin’s care, like keeping things straight or remembering what needs to be done. And I get why that bothers her. I mean, she’ll say something and I think I’ve got it, and then later I’m second-guessing myself.

And with the catering stuff—well, I’m not really working a regular job now, but when I do those small catering tasks, I’ve had to double-check myself or even redo things so orders or little details don’t get mixed up. It’s embarrassing, because it seems like it should be simple. Like labels, receipts, the count on trays—my uncle used to say, “measure twice, cut once,” though that was for carpentry, not sandwiches. But yeah, it does spill over beyond just me misplacing my keys at home.
Aside from these attention and memory issues, have you been experiencing ongoing sadness, loss of interest in things you used to enjoy, or excessive worry over the past several months?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say that’s been the main thing, no.

I mean, I get frustrated with myself, sure, especially when I’ve misplaced something or I’ve got to go back and check something I should’ve remembered. And worrying—well, everybody worries some, right? My wife can worry circles around me about appointments and family stuff, and then I start worrying because she’s worrying.

But ongoing sadness or not enjoying anything… I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I still like little things when I actually get to them. I guess I haven’t really been tracking my mood like that.
